title: Choose the dashboard composition
question: Which clinician workbench should carry Ovok’s visual identity? Choose the composition that makes CHF review feel clearest.

options.label: The Review Queue
options.thesis: Start with the patients who need a clinician’s attention today, then open their ECG, weight, and check-in together.
options.viewport: A slim Ovok rail anchors a spacious CHF workbench: clinic context and date above, a compact review summary, then a clear patient queue with reading type, time, and status.
options.risk: The queue must make its next action obvious without making synthetic readings look like clinical advice.

options.label: Signals Setup Register
options.thesis: Put the connected clinic and read-only Signals readiness in view, then guide clinicians into the patient worklist.
options.viewport: A fixed Ovok rail sits beside a project heading, a restrained Signals status panel with setup guidance, and a patient queue that keeps names and open readings visible.
options.risk: Setup can dominate the first screen unless status and next steps stay compact and clearly read-only.

options.label: Patient Measurement Review
options.thesis: Keep one patient’s recent ECG, weight, and questionnaire together so a clinician can understand the latest check-in at a glance.
options.viewport: A calm clinic rail frames a patient identity and latest check-in, followed by three aligned reading sections with timestamps, source devices, and a subtle history strip.
options.risk: The selected-patient focus may hide the breadth of today’s clinic work if the patient switcher is too quiet.
